We also ship the following extra classes:
DiscreteHilbertConstraint - Base class for implementing custom constraints

ExtraConstraint - Combine two constraints using logical AND
ExtraConstraint - Combine two constraints using logical AND
For more complex constraints or combinations of conditions, you’ll need to implement custom constraints as described below.
Do you need custom constraints?
Constraints are used in 2 places throughout NetKet.
To enumerate the full Hilbert Space, therefore when converting a NetKet operator to a numpy dense or scipy sparse matrix to perform exact diagonalisation.
To enumerate the full Hilbert Space, therefore when converting a NetKet operator to a numpy dense or scipy sparse matrix to perform exact diagonalisation.
To generate valid random configurations belonging to the subspace, used when initialising Markov Chain samplers.
To generate valid random configurations belonging to the subspace, used when initialising Markov Chain samplers.
In most serious VMC calculations, point 1 is not relevant because the system is too large to do ED anyway, and so you only really need 2.
However there are other, simpler methods of initialising MCMC samplers. For example, you could initialise them manually with a few valid configurations.
So, while it’s generally useful to implement your own constraints, you might not really need to do it.
